label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
**One star for now: our migration needs more than “escalated to engineering”**

Bridger Bend Community Library is a one-branch library with two full-time staff, volunteers, and about 2,300 active cardholders. We signed a three-year contract with Stackhouse Cloud in June 2026 at $14,200 a year. Our catalog and circulation migration went live October 19.

Since October 28, checkouts have worked only in offline mode on one laptop. Our holds queue was wiped out—approximately 640 holds lost. Our support ticket has been open for 12 days. We have received three replies, all saying the issue has been “escalated to engineering.” We still need a resolution and a clear account of what happens next.

These failures have consequences beyond staff inconvenience. A retired rancher drove 40 minutes to collect the large-print Westerns he had placed on hold. We had no record of his hold and sent him home empty-handed. A volunteer has been recording checkouts on index cards. With our county budget hearing on November 18 and our library’s line item on the agenda, we need to be able to explain both this expenditure and the plan to restore service.

During the sales process, we were promised “a dedicated migration specialist.” What we received was a shared inbox. For a library our size, that difference matters. We do not have an IT department to fill the gap.

To be fair, the software looked good in the demonstration, and the staff interface is better than our previous system. My concern is not the product idea. It is the support when essential services stop working.

I am asking for a named senior person at Stackhouse to call me this week, take responsibility for our case, and provide a written recovery plan, including whether our holds can be restored.

For other small-library directors: ask for support response times, escalation procedures, and migration staffing commitments in writing before signing.

One star reflects our experience today. I would revisit this review if Stackhouse resolves these problems and follows through on support.
